note: Known-good Windows driver packages (storage, NIC, laptop-input I2C) Beacon can fetch on demand (see services.drivers.fetch_pack and the Windows Drivers page). Beacon deliberately does NOT bundle these drivers - they are proprietary and not redistributable - so instead each entry pins a WHQL-signed driver CAB served by Microsoft's Windows Update CDN (discovered via catalog.update.microsoft.com) plus its sha256. The fetch refuses a file whose hash does not match, so a moved, replaced, or tampered URL fails loudly instead of staging unknown bytes. Every entry below was verified at pin time (storage/NIC packs on 2026-07-24, the Serial IO / AMD I2C touchpad packs on 2026-07-25) by downloading the URL, extracting it with 7z, and reading the INF: the PCI device IDs quoted in 'covers' come from the actual .inf contents. When updating an entry, repeat that verification and re-pin the hash. To refresh an entry (e.g. a new chipset generation): search catalog.update.microsoft.com for the driver ('Intel RST VMD' / 'AMD-RAID Bottom Device') - searching by hardware ID also works and is the precise way to find bus-driver packages ('INT34C5', 'AMDI0010', 'VEN_8086&DEV_A0E8'), take the update GUID from the result row, POST it to DownloadDialog.aspx as updateIDs=[{"size":0,"languages":"","uidInfo":"<guid>","updateID":"<guid>"}] to get the direct download.windowsupdate.com CAB URL, then download + 7z-extract it, read the INF's PCI\VEN/DEV list to confirm coverage, and pin the new sha256. Do not source from downloadmirror.intel.com: Intel discontinued the plain f6flpy zips, SetupRST.exe cannot be unpacked server-side (the payload is a .NET blob, not an archive), and the mirror requires an intel.com Referer and rotates download IDs. Beware coverage drops on version bumps: RST 20.2.4.1019 is the last build that includes 11th-gen 9A0B - newer 20.2.x builds silently dropped it, which is why there are two Intel entries. Entry fields beyond the basics: "target": "boot" stages into data/nicdrivers and bakes into every Windows boot.wim (NIC drivers - they must exist before the network does) instead of the SMB share; "include" limits which folders of a bundle zip are staged; "referer" is sent with the download (downloadmirror.intel.com refuses requests without an intel.com Referer). The exception to WU-only sourcing is the Intel Wired_driver zip: WU prunes its Win10-decorated NIC builds, and the zip's per-OS trees (NDIS68 = build 17763+, W11 = 22000+) are the only complete source; find current mirror IDs via Wayback snapshots of the Intel download page when the pinned one rots.

packs.title: Intel RST VMD
packs.covers: Every Intel VMD generation in one package: 11th-gen Core through Core Ultra Series 2 (device IDs 9A0B, 467F, A77F, 7D0B, AD0B + managed controller 09AB). The one to fetch first for Intel machines - later upstream builds dropped 11th gen.

packs.title: Intel RST VMD (newest build)
packs.covers: Intel's latest VMD driver - 12th gen and later only (11th-gen 9A0B was dropped upstream). Safe to stage alongside the package above: Setup PnP-ranks per machine, so each box gets the best matching version.

packs.title: Intel Ethernet NIC pack (baked into boot images)
packs.covers: Wired Intel NICs stock WinPE lacks: I225/I226 2.5GbE (NUCs, most 2020+ boards; no Server 2016 driver exists for these) and X520/X540/X550 10GbE (all PE versions incl. Server 2016). Baked into every Windows image's boot.wim and loaded before networking starts.

packs.title: AMD RAID (RAIDXpert2)
packs.covers: AMD SATA/NVMe RAID for machines with RAID enabled in firmware (AM4/AM5/Threadripper). The full F6 set: rcbottom (claims the disks), rcraid (the array controller), rccfg (configuration).

packs.title: Intel Serial IO (laptop touchpad)
packs.covers: Laptop touchpads are HID-over-I2C: WinPE has the touchpad driver (hidi2c) inbox but nothing for the Intel Serial IO GPIO/I2C controllers underneath it, so during Setup only a USB mouse works. One CAB per platform generation - Skylake/Kaby Lake (6th-7th gen), Cannon/Comet Lake (8th-10th), Ice Lake, Tiger Lake LP+H (11th), Alder/Raptor Lake incl. N-series (12th-14th), Meteor+Arrow Lake, and Lunar Lake - each verified to carry the GPIO2 and I2C INFs. Setup PnP-matches per machine, so staging every generation at once is safe.

packs.title: AMD I2C/GPIO (laptop touchpad)
packs.covers: The AMD side of the touchpad story: amdi2c claims the I2C bus every Ryzen laptop touchpad hangs off (ACPI AMDI0010/AMD0010), and the two GPIO drivers cover the interrupt controller across Ryzen generations (amdgpio2 for AMDI0030/0031, amdgpio3 for AMDIF030/031 on the newest platforms). With these staged, WinPE's inbox hidi2c driver brings the touchpad up when Setup starts.
